neutral_facts.value: The accused, Subodh Nath and Paritosh, were prosecuted for the killing of Ashutosh. The prosecution case was supported by the testimony of an eyewitness, PW-13, who stated that the accused assaulted the deceased with an axe and a lathi, and that the accused later shot the deceased with a gun. PW-13 fled the scene due to fear of the accused. The evidence of PW-13 was corroborated by PW-6, who found the deceased and the accused grazing cows in the jungle. The Investigating Officer recovered an axe handle near the deceased's body. The trial court convicted both accused under s.302/34 IPC, and the High Court upheld the conviction. However, the Supreme Court remitted the case of Paritosh to the Juvenile Justice Board as he was under 18 at the time of the offence, and acquitted Subodh Nath based on the corroborated evidence.

quotes.text: The trial court convicted the appellants under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'the IPC') and sentenced them to imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.5000/- each and in default, to undergo further imprisonment for a period of one year. The appellants filed Criminal Appeal No. 22 of 2004 before the High Court, but by the impugned judgment the High Court maintained the conviction and sentence and dismissed the appeal.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused were guilty of the offence under Section 302/34 IPC, supported by the testimony of an eye-witness, PW-13, and corroborated by other evidence such as the recovery of the weapon and the inquest report. They also contended that the motive to kill was not established, but argued that direct evidence of the offence was sufficient.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that appellant No.2 was below 18 years of age at the time of the offence and thus a juvenile under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, and that the 2000 Act should apply. They also claimed that the conviction of appellant No.1 was based on an unreliable sole witness, PW-13, who had run away from the scene and was a suspect, and that there were discrepancies in the evidence, lack of weapon recovery, and no established motive.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000, applies to offences committed prior to its commencement if the accused was below 18 years of age at the time of the offence. It also emphasized that discrepancies in witness accounts are not sufficient to discard evidence unless they are 'material discrepancies' creating reasonable doubt.
